comments.body:
## RE-SCOPED — my original filing was wrong on both counts. Corrected here.

A peer session challenged this ticket, I verified their claims, and they are right. Recording the
full correction rather than quietly editing, because this ticket was filed P1 and I propagated its
false premise to other agents.

### What I got wrong

**1. `--caused-by` is NOT absent or inert. It works.**

- `src/rebar/_commands/transition.py:123-124,150-152,164` — `_parse_flags` parses
  `[--caused-by[=]]` and returns it; documented as the explicit culprit (ticket 555e).
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_caused_by_autoderive.py:33`
  `test_explicit_caused_by_on_bug_close` drives `--caused-by={culprit}` **through the CLI** and
  asserts the resulting edge. It is green.
- The peer demonstrated it directly in a fresh store with **zero commits and no `file_impact`**,
  so `blame.derive_caused_by` was structurally incapable of producing anything — and the edge
  still named the flag's culprit.

**2. My "silently ignores unknown flags" experiment was invalid.**

I ran `rebar transition <id> open open --definitely-not-a-real-flag` against an already-open
ticket. That returns `no change: … already open` from an **early return**, before any close-path
flag handling. It never exercised a close, which is the only path where `--caused-by` does
anything. A bogus flag and a working flag behave identically on a no-op, so the experiment could
not distinguish them. Separately, `_parse_flags` documents that unknown tokens are skipped **by
design**, so that half is intended behaviour, not a defect.

### What IS real: two help sources for one verb, drifted apart

- `src/rebar/_cli/help/transition.txt` is what `rebar transition --help` renders. It contains
  **0** occurrences of `caused`.
- `src/rebar/_commands/transition.py:65` contains a SECOND help blob that documents it:
  `"  --caused-by=<id>         On a bug close, draw a caused_by link to the culprit change/ticket (overrides git-blame auto-derivation)."`

Both live in `src/rebar`. The commit that added the flag — `0f999860ad` (2026-07-19, ticket
`555e-3efa-4ad6-4169`, "555e: blame-derived caused_by on bug close + --caused-by") — added the
flag, the parser, the tests, and the `transition.py` help line, and did **not** update
`_cli/help/transition.txt`.

Verified this is not staleness on my side: the help line landed 2026-07-19 and my installed binary
is from today.

### Why it matters, at its true (lower) severity

The flag works, so nothing is broken — the cost is **discoverability**. An agent reading
`rebar transition --help` sees no `--caused-by` and reasonably concludes it does not exist. That is
exactly what happened to me, and I then propagated the wrong conclusion into instructions to four
other agents and into two other tickets. `docs/user-guide.md:194`, `docs/clone-guidance.md` and the
`/rebar-debug` skill all instruct passing it, so the rendered help is the odd one out.

This is the same shape as most of today's other findings: a change created an obligation (keep the
two help sources in step) and discharged it on one site only. It is **not** a correctness bug, and
P1 was far too high. Lowering to **P3**.

### Corrected Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar transition --help` documents `--caused-by=<id>`, matching the text already in
      `_commands/transition.py:65` — verified by a test asserting the rendered help contains it.
- [ ] The duplication is addressed at the root, not by copying the line into a second file: either
      one help source is derived from the other, or a test asserts the two cannot diverge for any
      flag the parser accepts. Copying the string leaves the next flag free to drift the same way.
- [ ] Every other flag `_parse_flags` accepts is present in the rendered help (`--reason`,
      `--class`, `--force`, `--ref`, `--caused-by`) — verified by a test derived from the parser
      rather than a hand-written list.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check`
      (`new=0 increased=0 stale=0`) pass.

### Withdrawn from this ticket

The unknown-flag-rejection criteria are removed: silent skipping is documented, intended behaviour,
and my evidence for it being harmful was an invalid experiment. If anyone wants to argue unknown
flags should be rejected, that is a separate design proposal and needs its own case.

compiled_state.description:
## Problem

`rebar transition` **silently accepts and ignores unknown flags**. Demonstrated on a real ticket,
no mutation:

```
$ rebar transition major-specified-bream open open --definitely-not-a-real-flag
no change: 50e3-6d2a-0e7f-4e92 already open
```

No error, no warning, exit 0. A misspelled or unsupported flag does nothing and says nothing.

## Why this is more than a nit: `--caused-by` is documented but not implemented on the CLI

`rebar transition --help` lists only `[--class=<value>] [--reason=<text>] [--force] [--force=<reason>] [--output json]`. There is no `--caused-by`. But it is instructed in at least three places:

- **`docs/user-guide.md:191-194`** — "explicitly with `--caused-by <id>` (which overrides the
  git-blame auto-derivation)", with a worked example:
  `rebar transition <bug> in_progress closed --class=regression --caused-by=<culprit-id>`
- **`docs/clone-guidance.md:15,18`** — "Supply `--caused-by` when an explicit link is preferable."
- **The `/rebar-debug` skill** (lines ~498-512) makes it mandatory: *"`--caused-by` on the close is
  not optional once you have an origin, even if you already linked one"*, and *"Pass the flag on
  the close every time."*

The library side exists — `_lib_writes.py:339` threads `caused_by=`, and
`transition_close.py:175` defines `_apply_caused_by` — so this is a **CLI surface gap**, not a
missing capability.

**Combined with the silent-ignore behaviour, the effect is that every agent following the
documented protocol believes it supplied a proven attribution while the system actually fell back
to blame.** The instruction and the outcome diverge, silently, on the exact code path whose purpose
is to make attribution trustworthy.

## Observed consequences, this session

Four bug closes today passed `--caused-by=<proven-origin>` per the skill. In each case:

- the flag was ignored;
- the `caused_by` edge that existed came from an earlier explicit `rebar link`;
- blame auto-derivation ran on close and attached a SECOND edge.

That mis-diagnosis was filed as `ruling-magnific-bats` (`10d0-c26c-bdbb-4b1f`) with the wrong
premise — "`--caused-by` adds a duplicate edge" — when the actual mechanism is "blame
auto-derivation adds an edge without checking whether one is already recorded". A correction is
recorded on that ticket.

Worth noting in fairness: in the observed cases **blame landed on the same origin the agent had
proven by hand**, so the duplicate was redundant rather than wrong. That is evidence about blame's
accuracy, not an argument that the gap is harmless — an agent that believes it overrode the
fallback has no way to discover that it did not.

## Two defects, and they should probably be fixed together

1. **Unknown flags are silently ignored.** A typo (`--forse`, `--clas=regression`) does nothing and
   reports success. Rejecting unknown flags is the standard contract and would have surfaced this
   in seconds.
2. **`--caused-by` is documented and instructed but absent from the CLI.** Either implement it
   (the library already supports it) or remove it from `docs/user-guide.md`, `docs/clone-guidance.md`
   and the `/rebar-debug` skill. Implementing looks strictly better: the whole point of the
   attribution step is that a proven origin beats a guess.

Fixing (1) without (2) converts a silent failure into a loud one — an improvement, but it would
break every documented invocation and every agent following the protocol. Fixing (2) without (1)
leaves the next typo silent. Consider ordering deliberately.

## Reproduction

1. `rebar transition <any-open-ticket> open open --definitely-not-a-real-flag` → `no change`, exit 0.
2. `rebar transition --help` → no `--caused-by` in the usage line.
3. `grep -n 'caused-by' docs/user-guide.md` → documented, with an example command.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An unknown flag passed to `rebar transition` is REJECTED with a message naming the flag, not
      silently ignored — verified by a test asserting a non-zero exit and the flag name in the error.
- [ ] The unknown-flag rejection covers the other mutating verbs too, or a reasoned decision is
      recorded for why `transition` is special — verified per verb touched.
- [ ] `--caused-by=<id>` on a bug close either works end-to-end (the recorded edge is the supplied
      origin, and blame auto-derivation does NOT also run) or is removed from
      `docs/user-guide.md`, `docs/clone-guidance.md` and the `/rebar-debug` skill. Decide and test
      whichever is chosen.
- [ ] If implemented: supplying `--caused-by` suppresses the blame fallback entirely, so exactly
      one edge results — verified by a test, and coordinated with `ruling-magnific-bats` (1973),
      which makes the `_apply_caused_by` write idempotent.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check`
      (`new=0 increased=0 stale=0`) pass.

## Provenance

Found while verifying a subagent's report that `rebar transition` has no `--caused-by` flag. The
agent was right and I had been asserting otherwise all session, including in instructions to other
agents.
compiled_state.title: rebar transition --help omits --caused-by: two help sources for one verb have drifted
